title: WPMS/7012/2001 of BALBIR SINGH Vs D.D.C/A.D.M/UPPER COLLECTOR HARIDWAR and ORS.

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
 MCC No.362/2020 (Review Application)
CLMA No.6859/2020 (Delay Condonation Application in Review Application on
behalf of the petitioner)
In
Writ Petition (M/S) No. 7012 of 2001
Balbir Singh ..........Petitioner
 Versus
Deputy Director of Consolidation Haridwar, Additional District
Magistrate/ Upper Collector, Haridwar & others

.........Respondents
Present:- Mr. A.K. Sharma, Advocate for the petitioner.
 Mr. M.S. Bisht, Brief Holder for the State.

Hon'ble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.
 This case has been heard through video
conferencing.
2. This writ petition was disposed of by this Court
vide order dated 06.08.2019.
3. Now a review application along with a delay
condonation application has been filed by the
petitioner/applicant for reviewing the order dated 06.08.2019.
4. Grounds shown in the affidavit appear to be
bona fide and sufficient for condonation of delay in filing the
review application. The delay condonation application is
allowed. Delay is condoned.

2
5. Heard learned counsel for the parties on the
review application.
6. It is an extremely old matter pertaining to bunch
of writ petitions which was filed before this Court. Part of the
writ petitions were pertaining to the ceiling and other
remaining writ petitions were regarding consolidation of
holdings. Since the ceiling was related to the same land in
question in village or villages, the matters were taken up
together.
7. The first bunch of writ petitions which was taken
up was regarding the ceiling, in which a detail order was
passed by this Court on 06.08.2019. The order dated
06.08.2019 which relates to the ceiling is a detail order where
the Court has held that there were fatal flaws in ceiling
proceedings as what was tenure-holder was not properly
appreciated by the authorities and the courts. The operative
portion of the order dated 06.08.2019 passed in Writ Petition
(M/S) No. 43387 of 1999 (New No.121A of 2006 and other
connected matters) reads as under:-
"42. In my considered opinion there has been a
fatal flaw in these ceiling proceedings. The twice
held proceedings have gone twice wrong in its
appreciation as to the actual "tenure holder".
Inspite of the flaws pointed out by the Allahabad
High Court earlier, the ceiling authorities have yet
again failed to appreciate the real meaning of
"tenure holder". A tenure holder would always
include the one who actually tills the land. In this
case it has been an absentee landlord, in the form
of an Agricultural Syndicate. The authorities have
merely taken into account what was there on the

3
revenue records, without appreciating the ground
realities, though there were judicial
pronouncements pointing out to the phony nature
of the "Agricultural Syndicate". The vital error
committed here is holding the "Agricultural
Syndicate" to be the "tenure holder" and then
determining the surplus. "Agriculture Syndicate"
was a ruse, created by a big landlord to save his
holdings, a reality which the ceiling authorities
failed to appreciate. Since there is nothing like an
"Agriculture Syndicate", it can never be treated as a
"tenure holder".
43. On the other hand, however, the present
petitioners have also not been able to show that
they are the ones who ought to be treated as
"tenure holder", as before the Prescribed Authority,
apart from their objections, no worthwhile evidence
was shown which could have strengthened their
claim as "tenure holders".
44. In the light of these findings the entire land
presently in dispute, must be declared as surplus
and shall vest with the State. This shall, however,
not include the land, where such appellants (under
Section 3(17) of the U.P. Imposition of Ceiling on
Land Holdings Act, 1960) were declared as "tenure
holders" as they had purchased this land in an
auction, particularly now when it was not
challenged further by the State Government.
45. The petitioners though have not been able to
establish their claim as "tenure holder". Yet each
claims to be still occupying an area of land which is

4
less than 7.30 hectare which would be within the
ceiling limits. Their claim, as already stated above
as tenure holder though has failed, all the same,
considering the small holdings each of them is
presently occupying, and as stated before the Court,
none has any other land except the present land in
question, the State Government shall examine each
case on its merits and if it comes to the conclusion
that save this land they would be landless, then it
shall allot the land in their favour in accordance
with law, subject to the limitation of Uttar Pradesh
Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1950.
 46. The writ petitions stand disposed with the
above observations and directions."
8. On the same day, consolidation matters were
also taken up and the following order was passed by this
Court:-
"These are all the matters which are connected
with the ceiling matter, which was taken up earlier
today as the leading case i.e. Writ Petition No. 121A
of 2006 (Old No. 43387 of 1999). These matters
have been decided by this Court holding that
though the petitioners have not been able to fully
establish their right as a tenure holder, but they
have been able to show to this Court that the one
who has been considered as tenure holder i.e.
Agricultural and Industrial Syndicate Company Ltd.
is actually a nonentity and should not have been
considered as a tenure holder.
2. It is also true that the petitioners are in
occupation of the land for some time and though

5
they have not been able to fully establish their
status as a tenure holder as defined under the U.P.
Imposition of Ceiling on Land Holdings Act, but the
fact as alleged by them is that they are extremely
small tenure holders having less than 7.30 hectare
which would be less than the ceiling limit and the
land, in any case, may be given to them under the
provisions of Section 198 of the Uttar Pradesh
Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act.
Therefore this Court directs the Collector concerned
to take a decision after hearing each and every case
and till a decision is taken the possession of the
petitioners shall not be affected.
3. This order, however, shall not restrict the
State Government to pass any appropriate order
considering the long standing possession of the
petitioners.

4. Meanwhile, it is hereby directed that after the
decision is taken by the Collector, the Deputy
Director of Consolidation shall re-appraise the
situation in the light of the decision of this Court
and take an appropriate action in each and every
case in terms of the Consolidation of Holdings Act.
Let the decision be taken by the Deputy Director of
Consolidation within eight weeks from the date a
decision is taken by the Collector.
5. With the observations as above, writ petitions
stand disposed."
9. The petitioner has not been able to show that there
is any error apparent on the face of record in the order dated

6
06.08.2019. The grounds for review are extremely limited and
even if one applies the principles as laid down under Order 47
Rule 1 of CPC, these grounds are not available to the
petitioner.
10. In view of the above, no interference is being called
for by this Court. Consequently, the review application is
dismissed.
 (Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
 29.10.2020
Ankit/
